有人问我w13scan和arachni的区别，之前没接触过，正好放假有空就看看这个扫描器。

Arachni是一个包含很多特性、模块化的、高性能的Ruby框架，目的是帮助渗透测试人员和管理者评估现代web应用程序的安全。Arachni是免费、源代码开源的，它支持所有主流操作系统

它是 ruby写的，地址是 https://www.arachni-scanner.com/ 它是可以基于webui来进行扫描操作。

扫描报告

不过我更关心的是它的扫描逻辑和payload，里面有不少模块值得w13scan学习，所以记录一下。

指纹识别

w13scan也有指纹识别的模块，路径是 W13SCAN/fingprints，也是收集自各个扫描器的，所以看arachni的指纹识别模块，只选取w13scan中没有的(现在没有，写完这篇记录之后就有了 = = )。

指纹都在 system/gems/gems/arachni-1.5.1/components/fingerprinters

用于识别框架，语言，操作系统和服务。

aspx_mvc 指纹识别

system/gems/gems/arachni-1.5.1/components/fingerprinters/frameworks/aspx_mvc.rb

言简意赅，从body，header，cookie中判断值。

ruby rack

symfony

  9. module Arachni
  10. module Platform::Fingerprinters

  12. # Identifies ASPX resources.
  13. #
  14. # @author Tasos "Zapotek" Laskos <tasos.laskos@arachni-scanner.com>
  15. # @version 0.1.1
  16. class ASPX < Platform::Fingerprinter

  18.     EXTENSION       = 'aspx'
  19.     SESSION_COOKIE  = 'asp.net_sessionid'
  20.     X_POWERED_BY    = 'asp.net'
  21.     VIEWSTATE       = '__viewstate'
  22.     HEADER_FIELDS   = %w(x-aspnet-version x-aspnetmvc-version)

  24.     def run
  25.         if extension == EXTENSION ||
  26.             # Session ID in URL, like:
  27.             #   http://blah.com/(S(yn5cby55lgzstcen0ng2b4iq))/stuff.aspx
  28.             uri.path =~ /\/\(s\([a-z0-9]+\)\)\//i

  30.             return update_platforms
  31.         end

  33.         # Naive but enough, I think.
  34.         if html? && page.body =~ /input.*#{VIEWSTATE}/i
  35.             return update_platforms
  36.         end

  38.         if server_or_powered_by_include?( X_POWERED_BY ) ||
  39.             (headers.keys & HEADER_FIELDS).any?
  40.             return update_platforms
  41.         end

  43.         if cookies.include?( SESSION_COOKIE )
  44.             update_platforms
  45.         end
  46.     end

  48.     def update_platforms
  49.         platforms << :asp << :aspx << :windows
  50.     end

  52. end

  54. end
  55. end

  9. # Extract paths from HTML comments.
  10. #
  11. # @author Tasos "Zapotek" Laskos <tasos.laskos@arachni-scanner.com>
  12. class Arachni::Parser::Extractors::Comments < Arachni::Parser::Extractors::Base

  14.     def run
  15.         return [] if !check_for?( '<!--' )

  17.         document.nodes_by_class( Arachni::Parser::Nodes::Comment ).map do |comment|
  18.             comment.value.scan( /(^|\s)(\/[\/a-zA-Z0-9%._-]+)/ )
  19.         end.flatten.select { |s| s.start_with? '/' }
  20.     end

  22. end

meta refresh

  1. class Arachni::Parser::Extractors::MetaRefresh < Arachni::Parser::Extractors::Base

  3.     def run
  4.         return [] if !check_for?( 'http-equiv' )

  6.         document.nodes_by_attribute_name_and_value( 'http-equiv', 'refresh' ).
  7.             map do |url|
  8.                 begin
  9.                     _, url = url['content'].split( ';', 2 )
  10.                     next if !url
  11.                     unquote( url.split( '=', 2 ).last.strip )
  12.                 rescue
  13.                     next
  14.                 end
  15.             end
  16.     end

  18.     def unquote( str )
  19.         [ '\'', '"' ].each do |q|
  20.             return str[1...-1] if str.start_with?( q ) && str.end_with?( q )
  21.         end
  22.         str
  23.     end

  25. end

script 中提取url

  1. class Arachni::Parser::Extractors::Scripts < Arachni::Parser::Extractors::Base

  3.     def run
  4.         return [] if !check_for?( 'script' )

  6.         document.nodes_by_name( 'script' ).map do |s|
  7.             [s['src']].flatten.compact | from_text( s.text.to_s )
  8.         end
  9.     end

  11.     def from_text( text )
  12.         text.scan( /[\/a-zA-Z0-9%._-]+/ ).
  13.             select do |s|
  14.             # String looks like a path, but don't get fooled by comments.
  15.             s.include?( '.' ) && s.include?( '/' )  &&
  16.                 !s.include?( '*' ) && !s.start_with?( '//' ) &&

  18.                 # Require absolute paths, otherwise we may get caught in
  19.                 # a loop, this context isn't the most reliable for extracting
  20.                 # real paths.
  21.                 s.start_with?( '/' )
  22.         end
  23.     end

  25. end

扫描插件

基于时间的代码注入

代码注入

  1. class Arachni::Checks::CodeInjection < Arachni::Check::Base

  3.     def self.rand1
  4.         @rand1 ||= '28763'
  5.     end

  7.     def self.rand2
  8.         @rand2 ||= '4196403'
  9.     end

  11.     def self.options
  12.         @options ||= {
  13.             signatures: (rand1.to_i * rand2.to_i).to_s,
  14.             format:     [Format::STRAIGHT]
  15.         }
  16.     end

  18.     def self.code_strings
  19.         # code strings to be injected to the webapp
  20.         @code_strings ||= {
  21.             php:    "print #{rand1}*#{rand2};",
  22.             perl:   "print #{rand1}*#{rand2};",
  23.             python: "print #{rand1}*#{rand2}",
  24.             asp:    "Response.Write\x28#{rand1}*#{rand2}\x29"
  25.         }
  26.     end

  28.     def self.payloads
  29.         return @payloads if @payloads

  31.         @payloads = {}
  32.         code_strings.each do |platform, payload|
  33.             @payloads[platform] = [ ';%s', "\";%s#", "';%s#" ].
  34.                 map { |var| var % payload } | [payload]
  35.         end
  36.         @payloads
  37.     end

  39.     def run
  40.         audit( self.class.payloads, self.class.options )
  41.     end

  43.     def self.info
  44.         {
  45.             name:        'Code injection',
  46.             description: %q{
  47. Injects code snippets and assess whether or not execution was successful.
  48. },
  49.             elements:    ELEMENTS_WITH_INPUTS,
  50.             author:      'Tasos "Zapotek" Laskos <tasos.laskos@arachni-scanner.com>',
  51.             version:     '0.2.5',
  52.             platforms:   payloads.keys,

  54.             issue:       {
  55.                 name:            %q{Code injection},
  56.                 description:     %q{
  57. A modern web application will be reliant on several different programming languages.

  59. These languages can be broken up in two flavours. These are client-side languages
  60. (such as those that run in the browser -- like JavaScript) and server-side
  61. languages (which are executed by the server -- like ASP, PHP, JSP, etc.) to form
  62. the dynamic pages (client-side code) that are then sent to the client.

  64. Because all server-side code should be executed by the server, it should only ever
  65. come from a trusted source.

  67. Code injection occurs when the server takes untrusted code (ie. from the client)
  68. and executes it.

  70. Cyber-criminals will abuse this weakness to execute arbitrary code on the server,
  71. which could result in complete server compromise.

  73. Arachni was able to inject specific server-side code and have the executed output
  74. from the code contained within the server response. This indicates that proper input
  75. sanitisation is not occurring.
  76. },
  77.                 references:  {
  78.                     'PHP'    => 'http://php.net/manual/en/function.eval.php',
  79.                     'Perl'   => 'http://perldoc.perl.org/functions/eval.html',
  80.                     'Python' => 'http://docs.python.org/py3k/library/functions.html#eval',
  81.                     'ASP'    => 'http://www.aspdev.org/asp/asp-eval-execute/',
  82.                 },
  83.                 tags:            %w(code injection regexp),
  84.                 cwe:             94,
  85.                 severity:        Severity::HIGH,
  86.                 remedy_guidance: %q{
  87. It is recommended that untrusted input is never processed as server-side code.

  89. To validate input, the application should ensure that the supplied value contains
  90. only the data that are required to perform the relevant action.

  92. For example, where a username is required, then no non-alpha characters should not
  93. be accepted.
  94. }
  95.             }
  96.         }
  97.     end

  99. end

ldap注入

  1. class Arachni::Checks::LdapInjection < Arachni::Check::Base

  3.     def self.error_strings
  4.         @errors ||= read_file( 'errors.txt' )
  5.     end

  7.     def run
  8.         # This string will hopefully force the webapp to output LDAP error messages.
  9.         audit( '#^($!@$)(()))******',
  10.             format:     [Format::APPEND],
  11.             signatures: self.class.error_strings
  12.         )
  13.     end

  15.     def self.info
  16.         {
  17.             name:        'LDAPInjection',
  18.             description: %q{
  19. It tries to force the web application to return LDAP error messages, in order to
  20. discover failures in user input validation.
  21. },
  22.             elements:    ELEMENTS_WITH_INPUTS,
  23.             author:      'Tasos "Zapotek" Laskos <tasos.laskos@arachni-scanner.com>',
  24.             version:     '0.1.4',

  26.             issue:       {
  27.                 name:            %q{LDAP Injection},
  28.                 description:     %q{
  29. Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (LDAP) is used by web applications to access
  30. and maintain directory information services.

  32. One of the most common uses for LDAP is to provide a Single-Sign-On (SSO) service
  33. that will allow clients to authenticate with a web site without any interaction
  34. (assuming their credentials have been validated by the SSO provider).

  36. LDAP injection occurs when untrusted data is used by the web application to query
  37. the LDAP directory without prior sanitisation.

  39. This is a serious security risk, as it could allow cyber-criminals the ability
  40. to query, modify, or remove anything from the LDAP tree. It could also allow other
  41. advanced injection techniques that perform other more serious attacks.

  43. Arachni was able to detect a page that is vulnerable to LDAP injection based on
  44. known error messages.
  45. },
  46.                 tags:            %w(ldap injection regexp),
  47.                 references:  {
  48.                     'WASC'  => 'http://projects.webappsec.org/w/page/13246947/LDAP-Injection',
  49.                     'OWASP' => 'https://www.owasp.org/index.php/LDAP_injection'
  50.                 },
  51.                 cwe:             90,
  52.                 severity:        Severity::HIGH,
  53.                 remedy_guidance: %q{
  54. It is recommended that untrusted data is never used to form a LDAP query.

  56. To validate data, the application should ensure that the supplied value contains
  57. only the characters that are required to perform the required action. For example,
  58. where a username is required, then no non-alphanumeric characters should be accepted.

  60. If this is not possible, special characters should be escaped so they are treated
  61. accordingly. The following characters should be escaped with a `\`:

  63. * `&`
  64. * `!`
  65. * `|`
  66. * `=`
  67. * `<`
  68. * `>`
  69. * `,`
  70. * `+`
  71. * `-`
  72. * `"`
  73. * `'`
  74. * `;`

  76. Additional character filtering must be applied to:

  78. * `(`
  79. * `)`
  80. * `\`
  81. * `/`
  82. * `*`
  83. * `NULL`

  85. These characters require ASCII escaping.
  86. }
  87.             }
  88.         }
  89.     end

  91. end

No Sql 注入（差分法）

  1. class Arachni::Checks::NoSqlInjectionDifferential < Arachni::Check::Base

  3.     def self.options
  4.         return @options if @options

  6.         pairs  = []
  7.         [ '\'', '"', '' ].each do |q|
  8.             {
  9.                 '%q;return true;var foo=%q' => '%q;return false;var foo=%q',
  10.                 '1%q||this%q'               => '1%q||!this%q'
  11.             }.each do |s_true, s_false|
  12.                 pairs << { s_true.gsub( '%q', q ) => s_false.gsub( '%q', q ) }
  13.             end
  14.         end

  16.         @options = { false: '-1839', pairs: pairs }
  17.     end

  19.     def run
  20.         audit_differential self.class.options
  21.     end

  23.     def self.info
  24.         {
  25.             name:        'Blind NoSQL Injection (differential analysis)',
  26.             description: %q{
  27. It uses differential analysis to determine how different inputs affect the behavior
  28. of the web application and checks if the displayed behavior is consistent with
  29. that of a vulnerable application.
  30. },
  31.             elements:    [ Element::Link, Element::Form, Element::Cookie ],
  32.             author:      'Tasos "Zapotek" Laskos <tasos.laskos@arachni-scanner.com>',
  33.             version:     '0.1.2',
  34.             platforms:   [ :nosql ],

  36.             issue:       {
  37.                 name:            %q{Blind NoSQL Injection (differential analysis)},
  38.                 description:     %q{
  39. A NoSQL injection occurs when a value originating from the client's request is
  40. used within a NoSQL call without prior sanitisation.

  42. This can allow cyber-criminals to execute arbitrary NoSQL code and thus steal data,
  43. or use the additional functionality of the database server to take control of
  44. further server components.

  46. Arachni discovered that the affected page and parameter are vulnerable. This
  47. injection was detected as Arachni was able to inject specific NoSQL queries that
  48. if vulnerable result in the responses for each injection being different. This is
  49. known as a blind NoSQL injection vulnerability.
  50. },
  51.                 tags:            %w(nosql blind differential injection database),
  52.                 references:  {
  53.                     'OWASP' => 'https://www.owasp.org/index.php/Testing_for_NoSQL_injection'
  54.                 },
  55.                 cwe:             89,
  56.                 severity:        Severity::HIGH,
  57.                 remedy_guidance: %q{
  58. The most effective remediation against NoSQL injection attacks is to ensure that
  59. NoSQL API calls are not constructed via string concatenation that includes
  60. unsanitized data.

  62. Sanitization is best achieved using existing escaping libraries.
  63. }
  64.             }

  66.         }
  67.     end

  69. end

响应头拆分

  1. =begin

  9. # HTTP Response Splitting check.
  10. #
  11. # @author Tasos "Zapotek" Laskos <tasos.laskos@arachni-scanner.com>
  12. # @version 0.2.3
  13. #
  14. # @see http://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/20.html
  15. # @see https://www.owasp.org/index.php/HTTP_Response_Splitting
  16. # @see http://www.securiteam.com/securityreviews/5WP0E2KFGK.html
  17. class Arachni::Checks::ResponseSplitting < Arachni::Check::Base

  19.     def run
  20.         header_name = "X-CRLF-Safe-#{random_seed}"

  22.         # the header to inject...
  23.         # what we will check for in the response header
  24.         # is the existence of the "x-crlf-safe" field.
  25.         # if we find it it means that the attack was successful
  26.         # thus site is vulnerable.
  27.         header = "\r\n#{header_name}: no"

  29.         # try to inject the headers into all vectors
  30.         # and pass a block that will check for a positive result
  31.         audit(
  32.             header,
  33.             submit: {
  34.                 follow_location:   false,
  35.                 response_max_size: 0
  36.             }
  37.         ) do |response, element|
  38.             next if response.headers[header_name].to_s.downcase != 'no'

  40.             log(
  41.                 vector:   element,
  42.                 response: response,
  43.                 proof:    response.headers_string[/#{header_name}.*$/i]
  44.             )
  45.         end
  46.     end

  48.     def self.info
  49.         {
  50.             name:        'Response Splitting',
  51.             description: %q{
  52. Injects arbitrary and checks if any of them end up in the response header.
  53. },
  54.             elements:    ELEMENTS_WITH_INPUTS,
  55.             author:      'Tasos "Zapotek" Laskos <tasos.laskos@arachni-scanner.com> ',
  56.             version:     '0.2.3',

  58.             issue:       {
  59.                 name:            %q{Response Splitting},
  60.                 description:     %q{
  61. HTTP response splitting occurs when untrusted data is inserted into the response
  62. headers without any sanitisation.

  64. If successful, this allows cyber-criminals to essentially split the HTTP response
  65. in two.

  67. This is abused by cyber-criminals injecting CR (Carriage Return -- `/r`)
  68. and LF (Line Feed -- `\n`) characters which will then form the split. If the CR
  69. or LF characters are not processed by the server then it cannot be exploited.

  71. Along with these characters, cyber-criminals can then construct their own
  72. arbitrary response headers and body which would then form the second response.
  73. The second response is entirely under their control, allowing for a number of
  74. other attacks.
  75. },
  76.                 references:  {
  77.                     'SecuriTeam' => 'http://www.securiteam.com/securityreviews/5WP0E2KFGK.html',
  78.                     'OWASP'      => 'https://www.owasp.org/index.php/HTTP_Response_Splitting'
  79.                 },
  80.                 tags:            %w(response splitting injection header),
  81.                 cwe:             20,
  82.                 severity:        Severity::HIGH,
  83.                 remedy_guidance: %q{
  84. It is recommended that untrusted data is never used to form the contents of the
  85. response header.

  87. Where any untrusted source is required to be used in the response headers, it is
  88. important to ensure that any hazardous characters (`/r`, `/n` and potentially
  89. others) are sanitised prior to being used.

  1. class Arachni::Checks::Xxe < Arachni::Check::Base

  3.     ENTITY = 'xxe_entity'

  5.     def self.options
  6.         @options ||= {
  7.             format:        [Format::STRAIGHT],
  8.             signatures:    FILE_SIGNATURES_PER_PLATFORM.select { |k, _| payloads.include? k },
  9.             each_mutation: proc do |mutation|
  10.                 mutation.platforms.pick( payloads ).map do |platform, payloads|
  11.                     payloads.map do |payload|
  12.                         m = mutation.dup

  14.                         m.transform_xml do |xml|
  15.                             xml.sub( m.affected_input_value, "&#{ENTITY};" )
  16.                         end

  18.                         m.audit_options[:platform] = platform
  19.                         m.source = "<!DOCTYPE #{ENTITY} [ <!ENTITY #{ENTITY} SYSTEM \"#{payload}\"> ]>\n#{m.source}"
  20.                         m
  21.                     end
  22.                 end
  23.             end
  24.         }
  25.     end

  27.     def self.payloads

  31.                 '/etc/passwd'
  32.             ],
  33.             windows: [
  34.                 '%SYSTEMDRIVE%\boot.ini',
  35.                 '%WINDIR%\win.ini'
  36.             ]
  37.         }
  38.     end

  64. parses XML input.

  66. This attack occurs when XML input containing a reference to an external entity is
  67. processed by a weakly configured XML parser.

  69. This attack may lead to the disclosure of confidential data, denial of service,

  9. # Tries to force directory listings.
  10. #
  11. # Can't take credit for this one, it's Michal's (lcamtuf's) method from Skipfish.
  12. #
  13. # @author Tasos "Zapotek" Laskos <tasos.laskos@arachni-scanner.com>
  14. class Arachni::Checks::DirectoryListing < Arachni::Check::Base

  16.     # The compared pages must be at least 75% different
  17.     DIFF_THRESHOLD = 0.75

  19.     def self.dirs
  20.         @dirs ||= [ "\\.#{random_seed}\\", "\\.\\", ".#{random_seed}/", "./" ]
  21.     end

  23.     def run
  24.         return if page.code != 200
  25.         path = get_path( page.url )

  27.         parsed_path = uri_parse( path ).path
  28.         return if parsed_path == '/' || audited?( parsed_path )

  30.         @harvested = []

  32.         dirs = [ page.url ] | self.class.dirs.map { |dir| path + dir } | [ path ]
  33.         dirs.each_with_index do |url, i|
  34.             http.get( url ) do |res|
  35.                 next if !res
  36.                 @harvested[i] = res
  37.                 check_and_log( path ) if done_harvesting?
  38.             end
  39.         end
  40.     end

  42.     def done_harvesting?
  43.         return false if @harvested.size != 6
  44.         @harvested.each { |res| return false if !res }
  45.         true
  46.     end

  48.     def check_and_log( path )
  49.         audited( path )

  51.         # If we have a 403 Forbidden it means that we successfully
  52.         # built a pah which would force a directory listing *but*
  53.         # the web server kicked our asses...so let's run away like
  54.         # little girls...
  55.         @harvested.each { |res| return if !res.ok? || res.code == 403 }

  57.         if !File.basename( @harvested[0].url, '?*' ).empty? &&
  58.             same_page?( @harvested[0], @harvested[5] )
  59.             return
  60.         end

  62.         if same_page?( @harvested[1], @harvested[0] )  ||
  63.             same_page?( @harvested[1], @harvested[2] ) ||
  64.             same_page?( @harvested[3], @harvested[0] ) ||
  65.             same_page?( @harvested[3], @harvested[4] ) ||
  66.             @harvested[5].code != 200 || @harvested[5].body.empty?
  67.             return
  68.         end

  70.         log vector: Element::Server.new( @harvested[5].url ), response: @harvested[5]
  71.     end

  73.     def same_page?( res1, res2 )
  74.         res1.code == res2.code && res1.body.diff_ratio( res2.body ) <= DIFF_THRESHOLD
  75.     end

  77.     def self.info
  78.         {
  79.             name:             'Directory listing',
  80.             description:      %q{Tries to force directory listings.},
  81.             elements:         [ Element::Server ],
  82.             author:           'Tasos "Zapotek" Laskos <tasos.laskos@arachni-scanner.com>',
  83.             version:          '0.1.7',
  84.             exempt_platforms: Arachni::Platform::Manager::FRAMEWORKS,

  86.             issue:       {
  87.                 name:        %q{Directory listing},
  88.                 description: %q{
  89. Web servers permitting directory listing are typically used for sharing files.

  91. Directory listing allows the client to view a simple list of all the files and
  92. folders hosted on the web server. The client is then able to traverse each
  93. directory and download the files.

  95. Cyber-criminals will utilise the presence of directory listing to discover
  96. sensitive files, download protected content, or even just learn how the web
  97. application is structured.

  99. Arachni discovered that the affected page permits directory listing.
  100. },
  101.                 references: {
  102.                     'WASC' => 'http://projects.webappsec.org/w/page/13246922/Directory%20Indexing'
  103.                 },
  104.                 tags:        %w(path directory listing index),
  105.                 cwe:         548,
  106.                 severity:    Severity::LOW,
  107.                 remedy_guidance: %q{
  108. Unless the web server is being utilised to share static and non-sensitive files,
  109. enabling directory listing is considered a poor security practice

  111. This can typically be done with a simple configuration change on the server. The
  112. steps to disable the directory listing will differ depending on the type of server
  113. being used (IIS, Apache, etc.).
  114. If directory listing is required, and permitted, then steps should be taken to
  115. ensure that the risk of such a configuration is reduced.

  117. These can include:

  119. 1. Requiring authentication to access affected pages.
  120. 2. Adding the affected path to the `robots.txt` file to prevent the directory
  121.    contents being searchable via search engines.
  122. 3. Ensuring that sensitive files are not stored within the web or document root.
  123. 4. Removing any files that are not required for the application to function.
  124. }
  125.             }
  126.         }
  127.     end

  129. end

  9. # HTTP PUT recon check.
  10. #
  11. # @author Tasos "Zapotek" Laskos <tasos.laskos@arachni-scanner.com>
  12. class Arachni::Checks::HttpPut < Arachni::Check::Base

  14.     def self.substring
  15.         @substring ||= 'PUT' + random_seed
  16.     end

  18.     def self.body
  19.         @body ||= 'Created by Arachni. ' + substring
  20.     end

  22.     def run
  23.         path = "#{get_path( page.url )}Arachni-#{random_seed}"
  24.         return if audited?( path )
  25.         audited( path )

  27.         http.request( path, method: :put, body: self.class.body ) do |res|
  28.             next if res.code != 201

  30.             http.get( path ) do |c_res|
  31.                 check_and_log( c_res, res )

  33.                 # Try to DELETE the PUT file.
  34.                 http.request( path, method: :delete ){}
  35.             end
  36.         end
  37.     end

  39.     def check_and_log( response, put_response )
  40.         return if !response.body.to_s.include?( self.class.substring )

  42.         log(
  43.             vector:   Element::Server.new( response.url ),
  44.             response: put_response,
  45.             proof:    put_response.status_line
  46.         )
  47.     end

  49.     def self.info
  50.         {
  51.             name:        'HTTP PUT',
  52.             description: %q{Checks if uploading files is possible using the HTTP PUT method.},
  53.             elements:    [ Element::Server ],
  54.             author:      'Tasos "Zapotek" Laskos <tasos.laskos@arachni-scanner.com>',
  55.             version:     '0.2.3',

  57.             issue:       {
  58.                 name:            %q{Publicly writable directory},
  59.                 description:     %q{
  60. There are various methods in which a file (or files) may be uploaded to a
  61. webserver. One method that can be used is the HTTP `PUT` method. The `PUT`
  62. method is mainly used during development of applications and allows developers to
  63. upload (or put) files on the server within the web root.

  65. By nature of the design, the `PUT` method typically does not provide any filtering
  66. and therefore allows sever side executable code (PHP, ASP, etc) to be uploaded to
  67. the server.

  69. Cyber-criminals will search for servers supporting the `PUT` method with the
  70. intention of modifying existing pages, or uploading web shells to take control
  71. of the server.

  73. Arachni has discovered that the affected path allows clients to use the `PUT`
  74. method. During this test, Arachni has `PUT` a file on the server within the web
  75. root and successfully performed a `GET` request to its location and verified the
  76. contents.
  77. },
  78.                 references: {
  79.                     'W3' => 'http://www.w3.org/Protocols/rfc2616/rfc2616-sec9.html'
  80.                 },
  81.                 tags:            %w(http methods put server),
  82.                 cwe:             650,
  83.                 severity:        Severity::HIGH,
  84.                 remedy_guidance: %q{
  85. Where possible the HTTP `PUT` method should be globally disabled.
  86. This can typically be done with a simple configuration change on the server.
  87. The steps to disable the `PUT` method will differ depending on the type of server
  88. being used (IIS, Apache, etc.).

  90. For cases where the `PUT` method is required to meet application functionality,
  91. such as REST style web services, strict limitations should be implemented to
  92. ensure that only secure (SSL/TLS enabled) and authorised clients are permitted
  93. to use the `PUT` method.

  95. Additionally, the server's file system permissions should also enforce strict limitations.
  96. }
  97.             }
  98.         }
  99.     end

  101. end

  1. class Arachni::Checks::OriginSpoofAccessRestrictionBypass < Arachni::Check::Base

  3.     HEADERS = [
  4.         'X-Forwarded-For',
  5.         'X-Originating-IP',
  6.         'X-Remote-IP',
  7.         'X-Remote-Addr'
  8.     ]

  10.     ADDRESS = '127.0.0.1'

  12.     def self.http_options
  13.         @http_options ||= {
  14.             headers: HEADERS.inject({}) { |h, header| h.merge( header => ADDRESS ) }
  15.         }
  16.     end

  18.     def run
  19.         return if ![401, 403].include?( page.code )

  21.         http.get( page.url, self.class.http_options, &method(:check_and_log) )
  22.     end

  24.     def check_and_log( response )
  25.         return if response.code != 200

  27.         log(
  28.             vector:   Element::Server.new( response.url ),
  29.             response: response,
  30.             proof:    response.status_line
  31.         )
  32.         print_ok "Request was accepted: #{response.url}"
  33.     end

  35.     def self.info
  36.         {
  37.             name:        'Origin Spoof Access Restriction Bypass',
  38.             description: %q{Retries denied requests with a spoofed origin header
  39.                 to trick the web application into thinking that the request originated
  40.                 from localhost and checks whether the restrictions was bypassed.},
  41.             elements:    [ Element::Server ],
  42.             author:      'Tasos "Zapotek" Laskos <tasos.laskos@arachni-scanner.com>',
  43.             version:     '0.1',

  45.             issue:       {
  46.                 name:        %q{Access restriction bypass via origin spoof},
  47.                 description: %q{
  48. Origin headers are utilised by proxies and/or load balancers to track the
  49. originating IP address of the client.

  51. As the request progresses through a proxy, the origin header is added to the
  52. existing headers, and the value of the client's IP is then set within this header.
  53. Occasionally, poorly implemented access restrictions are based off of the
  54. originating IP address alone.

  56. For example, any public IP address may be forced to authenticate, while an
  57. internal IP address may not.

  59. Because this header can also be set by the client, it allows cyber-criminals to
  60. spoof their IP address and potentially gain access to restricted pages.

  62. Arachni discovered a resource that it did not have permission to access, but been
  63. granted access after spoofing the address of localhost (127.0.0.1), thus bypassing
  64. any requirement to authenticate.
  65. },
  66.                 tags:        %w(access restriction server bypass),
  67.                 severity:    Severity::HIGH,
  68.                 remedy_guidance: %q{
  69. Remediation actions may be vastly different depending on the framework being used,
  70. and how the application has been coded. However, the origin header should never
  71. be used to validate a client's access as it is trivial to change.
  72. }
  73.             }
  74.         }
  75.     end

  77. end

  9. # WebDAV detection recon check.
  10. #
  11. # It doesn't check for a functional DAV implementation but uses the
  12. # OPTIONS HTTP method to see if 'PROPFIND' is allowed.
  13. #
  14. # @author Tasos "Zapotek" Laskos <tasos.laskos@arachni-scanner.com>
  15. #
  16. # @see http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WebDAV
  17. # @see http://www.webdav.org/specs/rfc4918.html
  18. class Arachni::Checks::Webdav < Arachni::Check::Base

  20.     def self.dav_method
  21.         @check ||= 'PROPFIND'
  22.     end

  24.     def self.found?
  25.         @found ||= false
  26.     end

  28.     def self.found
  29.         @found = true
  30.     end

  32.     def run
  33.         path = get_path( page.url )
  34.         return if self.class.found? || audited?( path )

  36.         http.request( path, method: :options ) { |response| check_and_log( response ) }
  37.         audited( path )
  38.     end

  40.     def check_and_log( response )
  41.         begin
  42.             allowed = response.headers['Allow'].split( ',' ).map { |method| method.strip }
  43.             return if !allowed.include?( self.class.dav_method )
  44.         rescue
  45.             return
  46.         end

  48.         self.class.found

  50.         log(
  51.              proof:    response.headers['Allow'],
  52.              vector:   Element::Server.new( response.url ),
  53.              response: response
  54.         )
  55.         print_ok "Enabled for: #{response.url}"
  56.     end

  58.     def self.info
  59.         {
  60.             name:        'WebDAV',
  61.             description: %q{Checks for WebDAV enabled directories.},
  62.             elements:    [ Element::Server ],
  63.             author:      'Tasos "Zapotek" Laskos <tasos.laskos@arachni-scanner.com>',
  64.             version:     '0.1.5',

  66.             issue:       {
  67.                 name:            %q{WebDAV},
  68.                 description:     %q{
  69. Web Distributed Authoring and Versioning (WebDAV) is a facility that enables
  70. basic file management (reading and writing) to a web server. It essentially allows
  71. the webserver to be mounted by the client as a traditional file system allowing
  72. users a very simplistic means to access it as they would any other medium or
  73. network share.

  75. If discovered, attackers will attempt to harvest information from the WebDAV
  76. enabled directories, or even upload malicious files that could then be used to
  77. compromise the server.

  79. Arachni discovered that the affected page allows WebDAV access. This was discovered
  80. as the server allowed several specific methods that are specific to WebDAV (`PROPFIND`,
  81. `PROPPATCH`, etc.), however, further testing should be conducted on the WebDAV
  82. component specifically as Arachni does support this feature.
  83. },
  84.                 references:  {
  85.                     'WebDAV.org' => 'http://www.webdav.org/specs/rfc4918.html',
  86.                     'Wikipedia'  => 'http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WebDAV',
  87.                 },
  88.                 tags:            %w(webdav options methods server),
  89.                 severity:        Severity::INFORMATIONAL,
  90.                 remedy_guidance: %q{
  91. Identification of the requirement to run a WebDAV server should be considered.
  92. If it is not required then it should be disabled. However, if it is required to
  93. meet the application functionality, then it should be protected by SSL/TLS as
  94. well as the implementation of a strong authentication mechanism.
  95. }
  96.             }

  98.         }
  99.     end

  101. end
